headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-file or manual handoff could enable prompt injection and data leakage, but ComfyUI is offline by default and ai-engineering-hub has no runtime I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can reference MCP/RAG topics and B has file-based inputs plus an asynchronous queue, so a shared workspace or manual handoff could let A’s content be treated as instructions by B. However, B has no clipboard or stdin/stdout bridge and A is not runnable, so this is not a default exploit path.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through a shared filesystem or copied prompt text
IF B parses A-produced text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require explicit human review before B consumes A output
Prefix A output as untrusted data in prompts
Disable any shared folder mount between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches images, videos, audio, seeds, and model artifacts, while A is an AI-engineering repository with no declared data classes. If they share a workspace, A-generated artifacts or prompts could be exposed to B’s file inputs, but B is offline by default and has no declared secrets handling, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory tree
IF sensitive prompts or assets are stored in files that B loads
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories
Avoid placing secrets in shared project folders
Review B’s loaded model/workflow files before execution
Use read-only mounts for any shared assets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or network capabilities and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The pair therefore lacks the overlapping mutable-resource access that would create a serious capability conflict.
conditions: IF A is given additional write or network permissions outside the profile
IF B is deployed with filesystem-write or git-write privileges not listed here
mitigations: Keep B’s filesystem permissions disabled
Do not grant A extra runtime permissions
Run both agents under separate OS users
Avoid shared mutable repositories

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an AI-engineering content source and B is a workflow-driven image generator; if B consumes A’s output as authoritative prompts or workflow text, errors can cascade into incorrect generations. B’s asynchronous queue and lack of built-in verification make this plausible, though not proven as a default behavior.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced text or workflows without validation
IF downstream users treat generated outputs as factual or final
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before B runs
Use schema validation for any A-to-B handoff
Log and diff A outputs before execution
Reject free-form instructions in workflow files

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile, and neither profile declares PHI handling or regulated data classes. With only docs-level evidence, there is no concrete compliance breach pathway to score above none.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes
IF a deployment introduces residency or retention requirements not shown here
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Review residency and retention settings
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Add a compliance checklist to onboarding
